candidates.rationale: Positive time-series covariance between a stock's daily trading range and its dollar turnover marks sessions where price discovery is backed by real capital commitment rather than thin, unconfirmed flow, so ranking that joint-activity magnitude separates durably well-supported names from ones whose volatility is a liquidity mirage.

When a stock's short-run liquidity rank sits persistently above its own multi-quarter liquidity standing, trading interest is building faster than its peer group's baseline, an attention shock that keeps drawing incremental flow before it is fully arbitraged into price.

Aggressive accruals mark earnings quality that invites scrutiny, so a simultaneous rise in day-to-day range volatility is more likely informed skepticism reaching the tape in a high-accrual name than the same choppiness in a clean-earnings one, ahead of the eventual accrual-reversal drift.

An overnight repricing visible at the very first print is more likely genuine information absorbed by a broad, liquid market when it lands in a heavily-traded name than the same gap in a thinly-traded one, where it is more often a single dealer's stale quote.

High-margin franchises sitting at a low percentile of their own year-long trading-activity range are under-monitored relative to their economic quality, and the liquidity gap closes as institutional attention normalizes toward the fundamental, re-rating price and turnover together.

Realized volatility earned per unit of a stock's own relative trading activity is a depth proxy: high values mean price moves a lot despite modest relative turnover, an adverse-selection signature that commands a return premium, while low values mark a well-absorbed, two-sided market.

Ranking a stock's own-history percentile of today's range, rather than its raw level or a cross-sectional comparison, isolates names currently in an unusual volatility regime relative to their normal behavior, and such regime shifts persist over the following weeks as the same catalyst plays out.

Statistically cheap-on-book names whose dollar volume has recently turned more erratic are undergoing a liquidity regime shift around a value-relevant name, and ranking the spread isolates the cheap stocks where that instability is most pronounced relative to how cheap they already are.

When a stock's price-volatility rank persistently exceeds its own share-volume-volatility rank, price is moving on relatively thin, inconsistent participation per unit of uncertainty, a latent illiquidity signature distinct from either raw volatility measure alone.

Averaging a stock's own trailing-month liquidity percentile over the past quarter captures sustained relative trading interest rather than a one-off spike, and durable attention of this kind is more consistent with gradual institutional accumulation that keeps building.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Downside-only return transforms don't rescue volume-return correlation: TS_CORR($volume, -MIN($return,0), 21) scored |t| 0.04, weaker than plain-return-volume correlations that already fail cheap_screen.
  2. A quarter of this round's rejects (5 of 20) were exact in-run duplicates, concentrated in earnings_per_share ratio/spread variants and close-low-high range ratios. Cross-check the run's own proposal list before submitting near-identical eps or range expressions.
  3. The high-low-range-over-TS_STD(high-low,10) chassis is now saturated: a window swap (21d, rho 0.972) and a denominator restructure (high minus TS_MIN(low,21), rho 0.915) both collapsed onto the archived CS_RANK(($high-$close)/(TS_STD($high-$low,10)+1e-8)). Stop deriving from this base.
  4. A bare 2-node fundamental RANK (e.g. RANK($roa)) can't serve as a crossover parent since it can't donate the required 3 shared nodes: both attempted roa fusions this round (x TS_CORR(high-close,return) and x return-mean-diff) were rejected as crossover_not_a_fusion.
  5. Any 'change' transform on $dollar_volume — TS_DELTA of the raw/LOG/TS_RANK series, or TS_CORR of TS_RANK($dollar_volume) vs its own DELAY — fails cheap_screen (|t| 0.13-0.38, 4 of 7 cheap_screen rejects this round). Use the level or TS_RANK of the level instead, which drove 4 of 6 accepts.
  6. CS_RANK($leverage) * TS_RANK($dollar_volume, w) scored |t| 0.08 on cheap_screen, far below asset_turnover/roa/roe crossed with the same volume-rank term, which produced this round's top fitnesses. Leverage is the exception to that template, not a safe substitute.
  7. CS_RANK($asset_turnover) * CS_RANK(-TS_MEAN($return, w)) is now saturated at w=5/10/21 (rho 0.81-0.85) even when a price-ratio term is grafted onto the return leg. Vary the fundamental or drop the return-mean leg; the window and the graft both fail to decorrelate.
  8. Within-run duplicates (the identical expression proposed twice in one round) were this round's single biggest rejection cause: 6 of 20 (30%), more than any one screen or correlation reason. Dedupe against this round's own batch, not just the archive, before submitting.
  9. CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($open, w)) * CS_RANK(TS_STD($open,63)/TS_STD($open,5)) shares 10 nodes across w=5 and w=10 (archive_subtree). This $open delta-times-volatility-ratio chassis is exhausted at short delta windows; the volatility-ratio leg's own windows are the untried lever.
  10. CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($roa, 63) - $accrual_gap) is itself a saturated 6+-node fundamental block — swapping only the second multiplicative leg ($high-$low vs TS_RANK($return,5)) still collides via archive_subtree because that prefix dominates.
  11. ABS($return) / ($dollar_volume+eps) style illiquidity ratios collapse onto plain TS_MEAN($dollar_volume) at rho 0.915. The volume denominator dominates the ratio; the return numerator adds little unless it's ranked or transformed independently first.
  12. Multiplying ($high-$low) directly by TS_MEAN($return,5) inside a fundamental cross barely fails cheap_screen (|t| 0.98), while subtracting a separately CS_RANKed TS_MEAN($return,5) from a separately CS_RANKed product clears easily (fitness 4.834). Keep return-mean legs rank-separated, not raw-multiplied, when fusing with a range term.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
